comprehension.prompt: In the test-tube cleavage experiment, lysate from cells given the Cas9 vector alone failed to cut the target plasmid. One other lysate in that experiment also failed. Which one, and what does its failure establish?

options.text: Lysate from cells given the guide RNA vector alone — establishing that the cutting seen in the other conditions came from Cas9 made in the cells, not from something else in the lysate
Lysate from cells given the guide RNA vector alone — establishing that the guide RNA is degraded when Cas9 is not there to protect it
Lysate from cells given both vectors but no extra guide RNA — establishing that assembly of the two is the bottleneck
Lysate from cells given Cas9 with a scrambled guide — establishing that targeting depends on the guide sequence matching

comprehension.why: The paper reports that lysate from cells transfected with the sgRNA-encoding vector alone did not support cleavage. Paired with the Cas9-only lysate also failing, that rules out the lysate itself supplying the cutting activity. Option b confuses this with the separate Northern blot finding that sgRNA is more stable when Cas9 is present; option d describes a control the paper never ran.

comprehension.prompt: When the researchers tested the lengthened guide RNAs, what drove their expression in the cells?

options.text: Two different promoters, U6 and H1, were each used
The same U6 promoter that had driven the original guide RNA
The CMV promoter, the same one driving Cas9
T7 RNA polymerase, as used to make guide RNA in a tube

comprehension.why: The original sgRNA was driven by the human U6 promoter. The 3'-extended versions were put under either the U6 or the H1 Pol III promoter — two promoters, not one. A reader who only skimmed would carry U6 forward from the earlier experiment and pick b.

comprehension.prompt: Two lengthened versions of the guide RNA were built. How did they differ from each other and from the original?

options.text: One added 4 extra base pairs to the helix and the other added 10; both also gained 5 nucleotides at the 3' end
One added 4 extra base pairs to the helix and the other added 10; neither changed the 3' end
Both added the same 10 base pairs to the helix, but differed in their 3' extension — 5 nucleotides against 10
One added 5 extra base pairs to the helix and the other added 20; both also gained 4 nucleotides at the 3' end

comprehension.why: The two designs added 4 or 10 base pairs to the helix that mimics the crRNA:tracrRNA pairing, and both were additionally extended at the 3' end by five nucleotides taken from the native S. pyogenes tracrRNA. Two changes were made at once, which is itself worth noticing.

comprehension.prompt: The Surveyor assay reports a percentage. What is that percentage a fraction of?

options.text: The cut fragments, as a share of the cut fragments plus the uncut PCR product
The cut fragments, as a share of the uncut PCR product alone
Cells carrying an edit, as a share of all the cells in the dish
Sequencing reads carrying an edit, as a share of all reads from the locus

comprehension.why: Percent cleavage was the average intensity of the 160-200 bp cleavage products divided by the sum of that and the uncleaved 360 bp product. It is a measure of band intensity on a gel, not of cells. Option c is what most readers assume 'editing efficiency' means, and getting that wrong changes what the headline number is a number about.

comprehension.prompt: The experiment that first detected cutting in living cells included a positive control. What was it, and where did it cut?

options.text: A pair of zinc-finger nucleases, aimed at a site neighbouring the one Cas9 targeted — not the same site
A pair of zinc-finger nucleases, aimed at exactly the site Cas9 targeted
A TALEN pair, aimed at exactly the site Cas9 targeted
Cas9 carrying a guide RNA already shown to work at a different gene

comprehension.why: A ZFN pair targeting a neighbouring site in the same locus was the positive control. 'Neighbouring' is the load-bearing word: the comparison the Discussion later draws between Cas9 and ZFN efficiency is between two tools aimed at two different sequences, not a head-to-head at one.

appraisal.prompt: The paper reports that the lengthened guide RNAs produced more cutting. How do the authors themselves characterise that conclusion?

options.text: As a suggestion, adding that more quantitative comparisons will be needed to confirm it
As a suggestion, adding that the experiment needs repeating in a second cell type to confirm it
As an established result of the study
As an established result, explained by tighter Cas9 binding that they measured directly

appraisal.why: The sentence reads: 'These results suggest that the 3'-extended sgRNAs support more efficient Cas9 function in vivo, although more quantitative comparisons will be necessary to confirm this conclusion.' Suggest, not show — and the authors name the specific thing missing, which is quantification, not replication. The abstract states the same finding flatly. Both sentences are the authors'; the difference between them is the lesson.

appraisal.prompt: Setting aside what the paper hopes for and what others later built on it, which of these did this study itself establish?

options.text: Cas9 and a guide RNA made inside the cell cut a chosen site, and the repair left insertions and deletions there.
Nothing yet firm. The cutting was detected by one assay only, and until an independent method confirms it the honest position is that the result remains preliminary rather than established.
That Cas9 cuts its intended site and no others, no stray cuts having been found elsewhere in the genome.
That editing is reliable enough in cultured human cells to justify testing it in primary tissue.

appraisal.why: The cutting is established, and by two methods rather than one: the Surveyor assay detected indels and Sanger sequencing of cloned amplicons read the mutated alleles directly. That makes b an over-correction, which is its own kind of misreading. c and d are the genuine overclaims: the genome was never surveyed for off-target cuts, and no primary cells or tissue appear anywhere in the paper. Being too sceptical about a demonstrated result is as wrong as being too credulous about an undemonstrated one.

appraisal.prompt: The paper is titled 'RNA-programmed genome editing in human cells'. Which statement matches the work the title stands on?

options.text: Editing at the CLTA gene in HEK293T cells: one locus, one line.
Editing at CLTA in HEK293T cells, and again at a second locus in the same line.
Cutting shown only in extracts from broken-open cells; the claim about living human cells rests on inference from those extracts.
Editing at CLTA across several human cell lines.

appraisal.why: Every experiment is one locus, the clathrin light chain gene, in HEK293T cells. Both halves matter: the gene without the line, or the line without the gene, leaves the claim looking wider than it is. c understates it in the opposite direction, and that is a real error too. The Surveyor assay was run on genomic DNA taken from living transfected cells; the lysate experiments were a separate line of evidence about what was limiting, not the basis for the editing claim.

appraisal.prompt: In the Discussion the authors compare their editing efficiency with zinc-finger nucleases. What do they report?

options.text: Lower than the ZFN pair used here, but within the range ZFNs and TALENs achieve generally
Higher than the ZFN pair used here, and above the general range for ZFNs and TALENs
About the same as the ZFN pair used here
Lower than the ZFN pair used here, and below the general range for ZFNs and TALENs

appraisal.why: Mutagenesis at CLTA ran consistently at 6-8%, which the authors state is lower than the ZFN pair aimed at a nearby sequence, though within the range seen for ZFNs and TALENs generally. They report an unfavourable head-to-head and then argue for their system on a different ground — that retargeting means rewriting a short RNA rather than engineering a new protein. Easier to aim is not the same as better at cutting, and the two claims sit side by side.

appraisal.prompt: The Surveyor percentage is computed from DNA pooled across the whole dish, including cells that never took up the plasmids. What follows for the headline editing figure?

options.text: With 30-50% of cells transfected, the rate among cells that got the machinery is roughly two to three times the figure reported.

Nothing can be concluded. Without knowing which individual cells were transfected, the percentage cannot be corrected in any principled way and should be read only as a lower bound of unknown looseness.
Nothing follows: untransfected cells contribute to the cut and uncut bands in the same proportion.
The figure already accounts for it, which is why the authors counted GFP-positive cells.

appraisal.why: Transfection ran at 30-50% with Turbofect, the reagent used for the experiments behind the reported figure, so most of the DNA in the denominator came from cells that never had Cas9 in them. The correction is approximate but it is a correction, which is why b gives up too early. c has the arithmetic backwards: untransfected DNA can only land in the uncut band. The GFP count in d is how the 30-50% was arrived at, not a correction applied to the result.
